findings.finding: The opening gives the partly replicated verdict and identifies Kupzyk (2011). The paragraph gives published and reconstructed power losses, cluster counts and empirical-versus-exemplary counts, with exact-replay limits and the remaining differences.

The paragraph begins with the partly replicated verdict and the scope of the new samples. It gives allocation and attrition loss estimates, the ICC pattern and the threshold and gap counts before moving into the planning background.

The planning question introduces formulaic, exemplary and empirical power in the context of the longitudinal trial. The design description, discussion of limitations and regeneration appendix supply the context for the technical comparisons.

The paper reports signed effect pairs 1.327/1.275, 4.391/4.472, 6.409/6.443, .454/.438, .851/.778, 3.037/3.062, 8/7 and 14/13 as in the packet. It gives the skewed-size rebound separately from the main ICC contrast and distinguishes the majority-centered last effect from the 41/54 and 40/54 counts.

The paper maps the four questions, the five main violation losses, ICC moderation, three changed thresholds, dropout oversampling, empirical/exemplary grids, fitted means, software examples, denominator comparisons and simulation precision to their respective claims.

The artifact table spans the chapters and Appendices A–D. The continuation retains the longer baseline run, the generator and GLS checks, both null settings and practical planning. The claim-map page labels for the threshold subsection, design section, initial empirical paragraph and precision illustration move with the new page breaks.
The paper distinguishes the observed-count denominator extension, independently averaged dropout masks and the proxy for the unavailable published Monte Carlo variances.

The paper identifies the original fitted records, random states and realized masks needed for replay. It separates threshold, rare-mask, denominator, reported interval and software-display explanations. Page 3 explicitly scopes the completers-only calculation and page 5 limits the refitting conclusion to the balanced baseline.

The in-house Satterthwaite calculation and its lmerTest comparator remain distinguishable, as do the Kenward–Roger procedure and its pbkrtest comparison. The discussion uses the checks to interpret the null and power results.
The simulation contrasts two fitted-analysis conditions and gives the paired effect and its Monte Carlo standard error while leaving general equivalence unresolved.

The title names Kupzyk (2011). The abstract attributes the allocation and attrition ranking, largest losses at lowest ICC, up to eight extra clusters and usual empirical deficit to Kupzyk. The citation jumps to the full dissertation entry on page 13.

The table separates signed effects, effect magnitude and direction. The footnote defines positive values, gives tolerances 0.001 pp, 0.002 pp and 0.5 for integer counts, and distinguishes descriptive effect comparisons from equivalence and stochastic uncertainty.
The Published cells give 1.3 and 4.4 pp mean losses from pp. 93–94 and Tables 1–2, with separate 1.27 and 4.47 pp Ours cells supported by the rerun paired contrasts.
The source prose on pp. 95–96 and Table 1 support the published 6.4, 0.45 and 0.85 pp losses. The rerun paired contrasts support the 6.44, 0.44 and 0.78 pp Ours cells under the matched designs.

Page 96 and Tables 1 and 4 support the published lowest-ICC peak and the .61-to-.67 pp skewed-size rebound despite the stated decline. The corresponding rerun grouping gives the same peak and the .56-to-.62 pp rebound. The displayed scalar compares the 15% dropout losses at ICC .05 and .15.

Published Table 5 has a largest eight-cluster increment above the between–within reference, compared with seven from the threshold rerun. The discussion on pp. 106–107 reports empirical power below exemplary in 41 of 54 cells; the saved rerun gap comparison gives 40 of 54. Each finding appears on its own side of the table.
